response: Yes, mammographic density has been shown to have an impact on the margin re-excision rate after breast-conserving surgery. Studies have found that women with higher mammographic density are more likely to require re-excision due to positive or close margins, as dense breast tissue can make it more challenging to accurately assess margin status during the initial surgery. This is because dense breast tissue can obscure the visibility of the tumor and surrounding tissue, making it more difficult for surgeons to achieve clear margins. As a result, patients with higher mammographic density may be at increased risk of requiring additional surgeries to ensure clear margins, which can lead to increased morbidity, cost, and patient anxiety.
